p.src: Now when Zhou Yu saw that Kongming had seized Nanjun, and then heard that he had also taken Jingzhou and Xiangyang, how could he not be enraged? His fury aggravated his arrow wound, and it was a long while before he revived. His generals repeatedly tried to console him. Zhou Yu said, “Unless I kill that village bumpkin Zhuge, how can I quell the resentment in my heart? Cheng Demou, aid me in attacking Nanjun; I am determined to recover it for the Southland.”

p.src: While they were discussing this, Lu Su arrived. Zhou Yu told him, “I intend to raise an army, settle once and for all who is stronger between Liu Bei and Zhuge Liang and ourselves, and recover the cities. Zijing, I hope you will assist me.” Lu Su said, “You must not. At present we remain locked in conflict with Cao Cao, and victory and defeat are not yet decided; our lord is now attacking Hefei but has not taken it; if we turn upon and devour one another, and Cao Cao’s troops exploit the opening to attack, our position will be perilous. Besides, Liu Xuande was once on close terms with Cao Cao. If driven too hard, he may surrender the cities and join Cao Cao in attacking the Southland. What then shall we do?” Zhou Yu said, “We devised the stratagems, lost troops and horses, and expended money and grain, yet he comes and takes the ready-made prize. Is that not hateful?” Lu Su said, “Gongjin, be patient for the moment. Allow me to meet Xuande in person and reason with him. If he cannot be persuaded, it will not be too late to take up arms then.” The generals said, “Zijing’s counsel is excellent.”

p.src: Thereupon Lu Su took his attendants straight to Nanjun and called for the gate to be opened. Zhao Yun came out to ask his business. Lu Su said, “I wish to see Liu Xuande and speak with him.” Zhao Yun replied, “My lord and the military adviser are in the city of Jingzhou.” So Lu Su did not enter Nanjun but hastened straight to Jingzhou. Seeing the banners arrayed in perfect order and the army presenting a magnificent appearance, Lu Su secretly admired them and said, “Kongming is truly no ordinary man!” A soldier reported within the city that Lu Zijing sought an audience. Kongming ordered the gates thrown wide open and received Lu Su at the government hall. After exchanging formal courtesies, host and guest took their appointed seats. When tea was finished, Lu Su said, “My lord, the Marquis of Wu, and Commander Gongjin have instructed me repeatedly to convey their meaning to the Imperial Uncle. Previously Cao Cao led a million men, ostensibly to descend upon the south of the Yangtze, but in truth intending to destroy you, Imperial Uncle. Fortunately, the Southland defeated Cao Cao’s army and saved you. Therefore all nine commanderies of Jingzhou ought rightfully to belong to the Southland. Now, Imperial Uncle, you have used a deceitful scheme to seize Jingzhou and Xiangyang, leaving Jiangdong to expend money, grain, troops, and horses in vain while you peacefully enjoy the gains. I fear this does not accord with reason.”

p.src: After the banquet, Lu Su took his leave and departed the city. He returned to camp that very night and recounted the whole affair. Zhou Yu said, “Liu Qi is still in the prime of youth. How can we expect him to die soon? When shall Jingzhou ever be returned?” Lu Su said, “Commander, set your mind at ease. Leave the matter to me. I shall make certain that Jingzhou and Xiangyang are reclaimed for the Southland.” Zhou Yu said, “What excellent plan have you, Zijing?” Lu Su said, “I observed that Liu Qi has indulged excessively in wine and women, and his illness has penetrated to his very vitals. His face is now gaunt, he gasps for breath, and he coughs blood; within half a year at most, he is certain to die. When we go to claim Jingzhou then, Liu Bei will have no excuse to put us off.” Zhou Yu’s anger had still not abated when a messenger suddenly arrived from Sun Quan. Zhou Yu ordered that he be admitted. The messenger said, “Our lord has surrounded Hefei but has gained no victory despite repeated battles. He has expressly ordered the commander to withdraw the main army and also dispatch troops to assist at Hefei.” Zhou Yu had no choice but to withdraw to Chaisang to tend his wounds, while ordering Cheng Pu to lead the warships and troops to Hefei and place them at Sun Quan’s disposal.

p.src: Now Liu Xuande, having gained Jingzhou, Nanjun, and Xiangyang, was overjoyed and began discussing plans for the distant future. Suddenly a man came into the hall to offer counsel. Looking at him, Xuande saw that it was Yi Ji. Mindful of the kindness Yi Ji had shown him in former days, Xuande treated him with the highest respect, invited him to sit, and questioned him. Yi Ji said, “If you wish to know a lasting plan for Jingzhou, why not seek out a worthy man and ask him?” Xuande said, “Where is such a worthy man?” Yi Ji said, “There are five brothers of the Ma family in Jingzhou and Xiangyang, and all are renowned for their talents. The youngest is named Su, with the style Youchang. The worthiest among them has white hairs between his brows. His name is Liang and his style is Jichang. The people of their district have a saying: ‘Of the Ma family’s five Constants, White-Brow is the finest.’ Why do you not seek this man and consult with him?” Xuande immediately ordered that he be invited. When Ma Liang arrived, Xuande received him with exceptional courtesy and asked him for a strategy to secure Jingzhou and Xiangyang. Ma Liang said, “Jingzhou and Xiangyang are exposed to enemies on every side, and I fear they cannot be held for long. Young Lord Liu Qi may be left here to recuperate, while former retainers are summoned and instructed to defend the region. A memorial should then be submitted appointing the young lord Inspector of Jingzhou, thereby reassuring the people. Then campaign south against the four commanderies of Wuling, Changsha, Guiyang, and Lingling, accumulating money and grain there to establish a firm foundation. This is a plan for the distant future.”

p.src: Xuande was delighted and asked, “Which of the four commanderies should be taken first?” Ma Liang said, “West of the Xiang River, Lingling is the nearest and may be taken first. Next take Wuling. Afterward, cross east of the Xiang River and take Guiyang. Leave Changsha until last.” Xuande accordingly appointed Ma Liang as an aide in his administration, with Yi Ji as his deputy; after consulting Kongming, he sent Liu Qi back to Xiangyang and had him relieve Yunchang, who returned to Jingzhou; he then mobilized troops to take Lingling, appointing Zhang Fei as vanguard, Zhao Yun to bring up the rear, and Kongming and Xuande to command the center, for a total force of fifteen thousand; Yunchang was left to guard Jingzhou; Mi Zhu and Liu Feng were left to guard Jiangling.

p.src: Now Liu Du, Administrator of Lingling, heard that Xuande’s army was approaching and consulted with his son Liu Xian. Liu Xian said, “Father, set your mind at ease. Though he has warriors as brave as Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun, our own province has Xing Daorong, a match for ten thousand men, who can withstand them.” Liu Du therefore ordered Liu Xian and Xing Daorong to lead more than ten thousand troops thirty li from the city and establish a camp with the hills behind them and the water before them. A scout reported, “Kongming himself is approaching at the head of an army.” Xing Daorong immediately led his troops out to battle. When the two armies had formed their lines facing one another, Xing Daorong rode forth wielding a great mountain-cleaving axe and shouted fiercely, “How dare you rebels invade our borders!” In the opposing formation could be seen a cluster of yellow banners. As the gate banners parted, a four-wheeled carriage was pushed forward. Within sat a man upright, wearing a silk headcloth and a crane-feather cloak, with a feather fan in his hand. Beckoning to Xing Daorong with the fan, he said, “I am Zhuge Kongming of Nanyang. When Cao Cao led a million men against us, I merely employed a small stratagem and slaughtered them until not a scrap of armor returned. How can the likes of you oppose me? I have come now to offer you amnesty. Why do you not surrender at once?”

p.src: Dao Rong laughed loudly. “The fierce battle at Red Cliffs was Zhou Yu’s stratagem. What had it to do with you? How dare you come here with your lies!” Swinging his great axe, he charged straight at Kongming. Kongming at once turned his carriage and withdrew into the formation, whose gate closed again. Dao Rong charged directly in, whereupon the formation swiftly divided and fled to either side. Seeing a cluster of yellow banners in the distance at the center, Dao Rong supposed Kongming was there and pursued only those banners. As he rounded the foot of a hill, the yellow banners halted, then suddenly parted down the middle. There was no four-wheeled carriage; instead, a general leveled his spear, spurred forward, and charged Dao Rong with a mighty shout. It was Zhang Yide. Dao Rong swung his great axe to meet him, but after only a few bouts his strength failed; he wheeled his horse and fled. Yide pursued close behind. Battle cries thundered, and ambush troops emerged from both sides. Dao Rong fought his way through in desperation, only to find a great general barring the road ahead and shouting, “Do you know Zhao Zilong of Changshan?”

p.src: Dao Rong knew he could not prevail and had nowhere to flee, so he dismounted and begged to surrender. Zilong bound him and brought him to the camp before Xuande and Kongming. Xuande shouted for him to be beheaded. Kongming hastily stopped him and asked Dao Rong, “If you capture Liu Xian for me, I shall permit your surrender.” Dao Rong repeatedly declared himself willing. Kongming said, “How will you capture him?” Dao Rong replied, “If the Military Adviser will release me, I have a cunning tale prepared. Tonight, lead your troops in a raid upon the camp. I shall aid you from within, take Liu Xian alive, and present him to you. Once Liu Xian is captured, Liu Du will surrender of his own accord.” Xuande did not believe him. Kongming said, “General Xing speaks no falsehood.” He therefore released Dao Rong and sent him back. Once released and back in camp, Dao Rong truthfully related all that had happened to Liu Xian. Liu Xian said, “What are we to do?” Dao Rong replied, “We can turn their stratagem against them. Tonight, station our troops in ambush outside the camp. Leave only empty banners standing within. When Kongming comes to raid us, we shall seize him there.”

p.src: Liu Xian followed the plan. Sure enough, during the second watch that night, a body of troops reached the camp entrance, each man carrying a bundle of straw, and all set fire at once. Liu Xian and Dao Rong attacked from both sides. The incendiaries retreated, and their two forces pursued them for more than ten li, until not one enemy soldier remained in sight. Liu Xian and Dao Rong were greatly alarmed and hurried back to their own camp. The flames were still burning when a general burst from within: it was Zhang Yide. Liu Xian called to Dao Rong, “We cannot enter the camp. Let us raid Kongming’s camp instead.” They therefore turned their troops back once more. Before they had gone ten li, Zhao Yun led a force charging diagonally from the side and thrust Dao Rong from his horse with a single spear stroke. Liu Xian hastily wheeled his horse and fled, but Zhang Fei came pursuing from behind, captured him alive from his saddle, and had him bound and brought before Kongming. Liu Xian pleaded, “Xing Dao Rong instructed me to act thus; it was truly not my own wish.” Kongming ordered him unbound, gave him clothes to put on and wine to calm his fright, then had him escorted into the city to persuade his father to surrender; if his father refused, the city would be taken and his entire household put to death.

He raised a white flag over the city, opened the gates wide, and carried the official seal and ribbons out to Xuande’s main camp, where he formally surrendered. Kongming ordered Liu Du to remain governor of the commandery, while his son Liu Xian was to go to Jingzhou and serve with the army. All the inhabitants of Lingling Commandery rejoiced.

p.src: After Xuande entered the city, settled the people, and rewarded the three armies, he asked his generals, “Lingling is ours. Who dares take Guiyang Commandery?” Zhao Yun answered, “I am willing to go.” Zhang Fei strode forward eagerly and said, “I too am willing to go!” The two contended for the assignment. Kongming said, “Zilong answered first, after all. Let Zilong go.” Zhang Fei would not accept this and insisted on taking the commandery himself. Kongming told them to draw lots, and whoever won would go. Once again, Zilong drew the winning lot. Zhang Fei said angrily, “I need no one’s help. Give me only three thousand troops, and I shall surely take the city.” Zhao Yun said, “I too shall take only three thousand troops. If I fail to take the city, I willingly submit to military punishment.” Kongming was delighted. He had Zhao Yun write a military pledge and entrusted him with three thousand picked troops. Zhang Fei remained dissatisfied, but Xuande shouted him back.

p.src: Zhao Yun led his three thousand troops straight toward Guiyang. Scouts soon reported the news to Zhao Fan, governor of Guiyang. Zhao Fan hurriedly gathered his officers to deliberate. The army commandants Chen Ying and Bao Long volunteered to lead troops into battle. Both men had originally been hunters from the mountain villages of Guiyang. Chen Ying was skilled with the flying fork, while Bao Long had once shot two tigers dead. Confident in their valor and strength, the two said to Zhao Fan, “If Liu Bei comes, we are willing to serve as the vanguard.” Zhao Fan said, “I have heard that Liu Xuande is an Imperial Uncle of the great Han; moreover, Kongming is rich in stratagems, while Guan and Zhang possess extraordinary valor. Zhao Zilong, who now leads the troops against us, moved through the million-strong host at Changban in Dangyang as though no one stood before him. How many troops can our Guiyang possibly muster? We must not meet them in battle; surrender is our only course.” Chen Ying said, “Allow me to go out and fight. If I fail to capture Zhao Yun, it will not be too late for the governor to surrender then.”

moreover, Kongming is rich in stratagems, while Guan and Zhang possess extraordinary valor.
Zhao Zilong, who now leads the troops against us, moved through the million-strong host at Changban in Dangyang as though no one stood before him.
How many troops can our Guiyang possibly muster?
We must not meet them in battle; surrender is our only course.”
Chen Ying said, “Allow me to go out and fight.
If I fail to capture Zhao Yun, it will not be too late for the governor to surrender then.”

p.src: Unable to dissuade him, Zhao Fan had no choice but to consent. Chen Ying led three thousand troops out of the city to meet the enemy and soon saw Zhao Yun approaching at the head of his army. Chen Ying drew up his formation, spurred out, and brandished his fork. Zhao Yun rode out with spear leveled and rebuked Chen Ying: “My lord Liu Xuande is the younger brother of Liu Jingsheng. He now assists Lord Liu Qi in jointly governing Jingzhou and has come expressly to pacify the people. Why do you oppose us?” Chen Ying cursed him: “We obey only Chancellor Cao. How could we submit to Liu Bei?” Zhao Yun flew into a rage, leveled his spear, and galloped straight at Chen Ying, who twirled his fork to meet him. Their horses met, and after four or five bouts Chen Ying knew he was no match; he wheeled his horse and fled. Zhao Yun pursued him. Looking back and seeing Zhao Yun’s horse drawing near, Chen Ying hurled his flying fork. Zhao Yun caught it and threw it back at him. Chen Ying barely dodged it, but Zhao Yun’s horse was already upon him. Zhao Yun seized him alive from his saddle, flung him to the ground, and ordered his soldiers to bind him and take him back to camp. The defeated troops scattered and fled. Back in camp, Zhao Yun berated Chen Ying: “With your paltry ability, how dare you oppose me? I shall not kill you today, but release you to return; tell Zhao Fan to come and surrender without delay.”

p.src: Chen Ying apologized, then fled ignominiously back into the city, where he told Zhao Fan everything that had happened. Zhao Fan said, “I wished to surrender from the start, but you insisted on fighting and brought this upon us.” He dismissed Chen Ying with a rebuke, then, carrying the seal and ribbons and accompanied by some dozen horsemen, left the city for the main camp to surrender. Zhao Yun came out of camp to welcome him, treated him with the courtesies due a guest, set out wine to drink together, and accepted the seal and ribbons. After several rounds of wine, Zhao Fan said, “Your surname, General, is Zhao, and mine too is Zhao. Five hundred years ago, we must have been one family. You are a man of Zhending, General, and so am I; thus we are fellow townsmen as well. If you would not disdain me, it would be my greatest fortune to become sworn brothers with you.” Zhao Yun was delighted, and each gave his age and birth date. Zhao Yun and Zhao Fan were born in the same year. Zhao Yun was four months older than Zhao Fan, so Zhao Fan acknowledged him as elder brother. Being from the same town, born in the same year, and sharing the same surname, the two became exceedingly close. When the banquet ended that evening, Zhao Fan took his leave and returned to the city.

p.src: The next day, Zhao Fan invited Zhao Yun into the city to reassure the people. Zhao Yun ordered his soldiers not to stir and entered the city with only fifty horsemen. The townspeople knelt along the road holding incense to welcome him. When Zhao Yun had finished reassuring the people, Zhao Fan invited him to a banquet at the government offices. When they were half-drunk, Zhao Fan again invited Zhao Yun into a secluded inner hall, where fresh cups were washed and more wine poured. When Zhao Yun was slightly tipsy, Zhao Fan suddenly summoned a woman to pour wine for him. Zilong saw that the woman was dressed in white mourning clothes and possessed beauty enough to overthrow a kingdom. He therefore asked Zhao Fan, “Who is she?” Zhao Fan replied, “She is my widowed sister-in-law, Lady Fan.” Zilong’s expression changed, and he treated her with respect. After Lady Fan had offered him a cup, Zhao Fan asked her to sit down. Zhao Yun courteously declined. Lady Fan took her leave and returned to the inner hall. Zhao Yun said, “Why trouble your sister-in-law to offer me wine, worthy brother?” Zhao Fan laughed. “There is a reason for it. I beg you, brother, not to refuse. My elder brother passed away three years ago. My sister-in-law has lived as a widow ever since, but that cannot be a final settlement, so I have often urged her to remarry. She said, ‘I will marry only a man who possesses three qualities: first, he must excel in both civil and military arts and be renowned throughout the realm; second, he must be handsome and dignified, with an exceptional bearing; and third, he must bear the same surname as my late husband.’ Where under heaven, you might ask, could such a coincidence be found? Yet you, honored brother, possess a stately appearance, your fame resounds throughout the four seas, and you bear the same surname as my elder brother. You meet her conditions exactly. If you do not find my sister-in-law too plain, I should like to provide her dowry and give her to you as your wife, binding our families for generations. What do you say?”

p.src: Hearing this, Zhao Yun sprang up in fury and cried sternly, “Since you and I have sworn brotherhood, your sister-in-law is my sister-in-law. How could we commit such an outrage against human relations?” Zhao Fan flushed with shame and replied, “I treated you with the best intentions. How can you be so discourteous?” He then glanced at the attendants on either side, intending to harm Zhao Yun. Zhao Yun had already perceived his intent. He knocked Zhao Fan down with one punch, strode straight out of the residence, mounted his horse, and left the city.

p.src: Zhao Fan hastily summoned Chen Ying and Bao Long to confer. Chen Ying said, “He has left in a rage. Our only course is to fight him.” Zhao Fan said, “But I fear we cannot defeat him.” Bao Long said, “The two of us will feign surrender and enter his camp. Your Excellency can then lead out the troops and challenge him, whereupon we shall seize him on the battlefield.” Chen Ying said, “We must take some troops with us.” Bao Long replied, “Five hundred horsemen will suffice.”

p.src: That night, the two men led five hundred soldiers straight to Zhao Yun’s camp and offered their surrender. Zhao Yun already knew in his heart that their surrender was false, but ordered them admitted. The two officers came before his tent and said, “Zhao Fan intended to ensnare you, General, with a beautiful woman. He meant to wait until you were drunk, have you helped into the inner hall, and murder you there, then take your head to Chancellor Cao and claim merit. Such conduct is utterly inhumane. When we saw you leave in anger, we knew that we would surely be implicated, and therefore came to surrender.” Zhao Yun pretended to be delighted, set out wine, and drank heartily with the pair. When both were thoroughly drunk, Zhao Yun had them bound inside the tent. He then seized and questioned their followers, and learned that it was indeed a false surrender. Zhao Yun summoned the five hundred soldiers, gave each of them wine and food, and proclaimed, “Those who sought to harm me were Chen Ying and Bao Long; none of you bears any blame. If you obey my plan, you shall all be richly rewarded.” The soldiers bowed their thanks, and the two surrendered officers, Chen Ying and Bao Long, were beheaded at once. The five hundred soldiers were then ordered to lead the way, while Zhao Yun followed with a thousand troops. Marching through the night, they reached the walls of Guiyang and called for the gates to be opened.

p.src: Those atop the walls heard them announce that Generals Chen and Bao had killed Zhao Yun and returned with the troops, and that they wished to consult the governor on official business. The defenders shone torches down and saw that they were indeed their own troops. Zhao Fan hurried out of the city. Zhao Yun shouted for his attendants to seize him, then entered the city, pacified the people, and sent an urgent report to Xuande. Xuande and Kongming personally hastened to Guiyang. Zhao Yun welcomed them into the city and thrust Zhao Fan down before the steps. When Kongming questioned him, Zhao Fan gave a full account of his proposal to marry his sister-in-law to Zhao Yun. Kongming said to Zhao Yun, “This too would have been a happy affair. Why did you act as you did?” Zhao Yun replied, “Zhao Fan had sworn brotherhood with me. If I were now to marry his sister-in-law, people would revile me. That is the first reason. If the woman remarried, she would forfeit her great chastity. That is the second. Zhao Fan had only just surrendered, and his true intentions were difficult to fathom. That is the third. My lord has only recently secured the regions of the Yangzi and Han, and cannot yet rest easy. How could I dare neglect my lord’s great enterprise for the sake of one woman?” Xuande said, “Now that the great enterprise is settled, what if I arrange the marriage for you?” Zhao Yun replied, “There is no shortage of women in the world. I fear only that I may fail to establish an honorable name; why should I worry that I shall find no wife?” Xuande exclaimed, “Zilong is a true man!” He thereupon released Zhao Fan and retained him as governor of Guiyang, while bestowing rich rewards upon Zhao Yun.
